title: reflog and stash
summary: Every place HEAD has been is in the reflog, so committed work is almost never lost. Stash parks unfinished work.

steps.title: The reflog: Git's flight recorder
body: Each time HEAD moves (commit, reset, switch, rebase, amend), Git appends a line to the **reflog**:
```text
$ git reflog
4e5f6a7 HEAD@{0}: reset: moving to HEAD~2
9c8d7e6 HEAD@{1}: commit: Add discount codes
2b3c4d5 HEAD@{2}: commit: Validate cart
4e5f6a7 HEAD@{3}: switch: moving from main to cart
`HEAD@{n}` means *where HEAD was n moves ago*. So after a bad `reset --hard`, the commit you "lost" is right there:
```text
git reset --hard HEAD@{1}        # or: git reset --hard 9c8d7e6
git branch rescue 9c8d7e6        # or keep it on a new branch
The reflog is **local** (never pushed) and entries expire after about 90 days. Unreachable commits are only deleted by garbage collection after that.

steps.prompt: Given the reflog above, which hash do you pass to `git reset --hard` to get back to the state just before the bad reset? (Just the hash.)
code: 4e5f6a7 HEAD@{3}: switch: moving from main to cart
steps.explain: `HEAD@{0}` is the result of the reset. One move earlier, `HEAD@{1}`, is where you were before it: the commit *Add discount codes*, which still has *Validate cart* as its parent.

steps.prompt: You ran `git reset --hard HEAD~3` on your feature branch by mistake. Arrange the recovery.
lines: Find the line just below `reset: moving to HEAD~3`
steps.explain: Read the reflog, identify the entry before the reset, move the branch back there, and confirm the commits are back.

steps.prompt: Which of these can the reflog **not** recover?
options: Edits you never committed, after `git reset --hard`
The old version of a commit you amended
Commits on a branch you deleted with `git branch -D`
steps.explain: The reflog records commit positions. Uncommitted work was never a commit. A deleted branch's commits are still reachable via `HEAD@{n}` entries from when you had it checked out.

steps.title: stash: park unfinished work
body: You are mid-change and an urgent bug report arrives. Your work is not ready to commit, and switching would clash. **Stash** it:
```text
git stash push -m "half-done coupons"   # save index + tracked edits, clean the tree
git switch main                          # fix the bug, commit
git switch coupons
git stash pop                            # re-apply the newest stash and drop it
| Command | Does |
| `git stash` / `git stash push -m msg` | save tracked changes, reset to HEAD |
| `git stash -u` | also include untracked files |
| `git stash list` | `stash@{0}` is the newest |
| `git stash apply` | re-apply, keep the stash |
| `git stash pop` | re-apply and drop it (kept if there is a conflict) |
| `git stash drop` | delete a stash |
Stashes are a stack: the newest is `stash@{0}`.

steps.prompt: You run these commands in order. What does `git stash list` print? Use the messages only, like `stash@{0}: On main: msg`.
steps.explain: A stack: `pop` removes the newest (`third`), and the remaining ones are renumbered from 0.

steps.prompt: You created `Coupon.cs` (never added) and edited `Cart.cs`. You run plain `git stash`. What is in your working tree afterwards?
options: `Coupon.cs` is still there; `Cart.cs` is back to its committed version
Both files are back to committed state and `Coupon.cs` is gone
steps.explain: By default stash saves tracked changes only. Use `git stash -u` to stash untracked files too.

steps.prompt: Match the command to its effect.
pairs: list every recent position of HEAD
re-apply the newest stash and remove it
re-apply a stash but keep it
put a name on a lost commit

steps.title: Find the commit before a reset
steps.prompt: A rescue script reads `git reflog` (newest first). Write `BeforeLastReset(List<string> reflog)` that returns the hash HEAD had **just before the most recent reset**: find the first (newest) line containing `": reset: "` and return the hash (first word) of the line **after** it. Return `""` if there is no reset, or nothing after it.
hints: Loop with an index so you can look at `reflog[i + 1]`.
template: "ccccccc HEAD@{0}: commit: More work", "aaaaaaa HEAD@{1}: reset: moving to HEAD~1",
"bbbbbbb HEAD@{2}: commit: Oops", "aaaaaaa HEAD@{3}: reset: moving to HEAD~5", "ddddddd HEAD@{4}: commit: old" }));
Dojo.Eq("no reset", "", BeforeLastReset(new() { "1111111 HEAD@{0}: commit: x" }));
Dojo.Eq("a commit message mentioning reset is not a reset", "", BeforeLastReset(new() { "1111111 HEAD@{0}: commit: Fix password reset" }));
